mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past month indicates a tightening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease > 0.5pp does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the past two months signals strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase > 5% does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past two months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face production challenges.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease > 1% does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% annualized over the past two months, the combined effect signals a tightening monetary policy and inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the past month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points, the combined effect signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k in 1 month and UNRATE decrease > 0.3pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.3pp does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% over the past six months signals robust consumer demand, which is a strong indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS increase > 5% does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and GDP (GDPC1) growth is above 2% over the past six months, the combined effect signals accommodative monetary policy with strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and GDPC1 growth > 2% in 6 months
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with strong economic growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS < 1% and GDPC1 growth > 2% does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.
